title: Chapter 1: I can do this
subtitle: Electromagnetic radiation
prac_text: Prac done and written up in my log book

rows.text: Recognise wave motion and give examples
rows.question:
Decide if the following statements are true (T) or false (F).
Visible light is an example of a transverse wave.
rows.question_note: Cambridge stem says statements (plural) because Q14 has seven parts; only part d is used. Kept as is.

rows.text: Understand that wave motion transfers energy without transferring matter
rows.question: Which of the following characteristics is particularly associated with wave motion?
options: vibrations which are longitudinal to the direction of motion
the transfer of matter from one place to another
vibrations which transfer energy from one place to another
vibrations which are transverse to the direction of motion

rows.text: Distinguish between transverse and longitudinal waves
rows.question:
Classify the following wave types as transverse or longitudinal waves.
sound waves, light waves, ‘Mexican’ waves, ripples in a pond, waves on a guitar string
rows.answer: Longitudinal: sound. Transverse: light, Mexican waves, ripples in a pond, waves on a guitar string.

rows.text: Use amplitude ($A$), speed ($v$), frequency ($f$), period ($T$) and wavelength ($\lambda$) to describe the motion of waves
rows.stem: A surfer sits on her board waiting for a set of waves to pass. Six waves pass her in a time of one minute, each of amplitude 1.5 m.
rows.question: Calculate the period of the waves.

rows.text: Explain the wavelength of a wave as a result of the velocity (determined by the medium through which it travels) and the frequency (determined by the source)
rows.question: What determines the speed of a wave?

rows.text: Solve numerical problems using: $\lambda = \frac{v}{f} = vT$
rows.stem: A surfer sits on her board waiting for a set of waves to pass. Six waves pass her in a time of one minute, each of amplitude 1.5 m.
rows.question: The waves are separated by a horizontal distance of 15 m. Calculate the speed of the waves.

rows.text: Describe all electromagnetic waves as transverse vibrations of electric and magnetic fields that travel at speed, $c$, in a vacuum
rows.question: Which one of the following is true of all electromagnetic radiation in a vacuum?
options: It is a transverse wave motion.
It travels at $3.00 \times 10^{8}\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.
It requires a medium to propagate.
Both A and B.
rows.notation_flag: Option B uses m s⁻¹ (Cambridge's text, kept as is pending Rocco's decision).

rows.text: Describe electromagnetic radiation emitted from the Sun as mainly UV, visible and IR
rows.question: The electromagnetic radiation from the Sun is comprises approximately
options: mainly visible wavelengths.
equal amounts of visible and IR wavelengths.
equal parts of UV, visible and IR wavelengths.
equal parts of UV and visible wavelengths.

rows.text: Recall approximate wavelength and frequency ranges of the radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray and gamma ray regions
rows.question: Arrange the following components of visible light in order of increasing wavelength: yellow, green, violet, red.

rows.text: Give examples of the different societal uses of regions of the electromagnetic spectrum from radio through to gamma rays
rows.question: List two or more societal uses of electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths in the range 700 nm to 1 mm.
rows.answer: Infrared. Any two: thermal imaging, night vision, remote controls, heat lamps, IR astronomy, optical fibre signals

rows.text: Use a ray model with wave crests to describe reflection and refraction of light
rows.question: When light waves refract at a surface between two different media, the wave crests change
options: direction and wavelength but not speed.
direction but not speed.
frequency and wavelength.
direction and speed.

rows.text: Define refractive index of transparent substances
rows.question: Define the refractive index, $n$, of a transparent medium.
rows.answer: $n = \frac{c}{v}$: the speed of light in a vacuum divided by the speed of light in the medium

rows.text: Use the equation: $n_1v_1 = n_2v_2$
rows.question: When a light ray moves from a medium with $n$ = 1.2 into a medium with $n$ = 1.6, the
options: speed, wavelength and frequency all increase.
speed decreases, the frequency is unchanged and the wavelength decreases.
speed is unchanged, but the wavelength and frequency decrease.
speed and frequency are unchanged, but the wavelength increases.

rows.text: Carry out practical investigations involving Snell's law
rows.prac: Practical 1C-1: Finding the refractive index of an unknown material

rows.text: Apply Snell's law to analyse qualitative and quantitative refraction situations of visible light
rows.question: A monochromatic ray of light passes through a glass prism as shown.
rows.question2: Which of the following is closest to the refractive index of the glass used in the prism?

rows.text: Qualitatively, using a ray model, explain the formation of images
rows.question: Use the diagram below to explain the way that the light rays form an image of the pencil at point Y.
rows.answer: Rays from X refract away from the normal as they leave the water. The eye traces them back in straight lines to Y, so the end of the pencil appears at Y.

rows.text: Carry out practical investigations involving total and partial internal reflection
Apply Snell's law to predict the critical angle at media interfaces
rows.question: A ray of light in an optical fibre travels down the core ($n$ = 1.58) of the fibre. The cladding has a refractive index of 1.55.
rows.question2: Which of the following is closest to the value of the critical angle for this light ray travelling from the core to the cladding?

rows.text: Carry out practical investigations involving dispersion of visible light
Qualitatively analyse situations involving dispersion of visible light in prisms and lenses
rows.question: Which of the following best explains why colour dispersion occurs in a glass prism?
options: the equal bending of all colours of light when they travel through the prism
the effect of differing speeds of the different colours causing different colours to leave the glass faster
the differing wavelengths of the different colours causing different amounts of light bending in glass
the slowing down of light in glass

rows.text: Qualitatively explain the formation of rainbows and mirages using a ray model of light
rows.question: The primary rainbow is best viewed
options: facing the Sun so it forms a bow around the Sun.
with your back to the Sun so that raindrops reflect light from their outer surface towards you.
facing the Sun so that sunlight can disperse into the colours of the spectrum.
with your back to the Sun so that sunlight can be dispersed and reflected back towards you.

rows.text: Apply Snell's law to analyse qualitatively and quantitatively the operation of optical fibres for communication
rows.question: What is the name of the optical principle that ensures light signals remain inside the core of an optical fibre?
